<a id="gamedataprivacy"></a>

## `GameDataPrivacy`

static class · `CwyLs.ModLoader.Core.Data.GameDataPrivacy` · assembly `CwyLs.ModLoader.Core`

The bus's redaction rules, as pure functions so they can be unit-tested without the game.

The snapshot is a plain text file on disk that other processes - and, through a mod, a remote LLM - are meant to read. Anything that identifies the machine or the human rather than describing the play session is filtered here, once, instead of being trusted to every call site.

<a id="gamedataprivacy--applytextpolicy"></a>

### `static string ApplyTextPolicy(string text, bool include)`

Applies the `Data.IncludeNoteText` switch to a body of free text (a note page, a diary entry). Text the player wrote is the most sensitive thing in the save file and also the thing an assistant most needs, so it is a single explicit switch rather than a per-call decision.

**Parameters**

- `text`: The text as the game holds it.
- `include`: The value of the config switch.

**Returns:** `text` when `include` is true, otherwise `null`. `null` means "withheld"; an empty string means "the player wrote nothing".

<a id="gamedataprivacy--redactaccount"></a>

### `static AccountView RedactAccount(string deviceId)`

Reduces the game's `AccountData` to a non-identifying flag.

**Parameters**

- `deviceId`: The game's `AccountData.DeviceID`. It is a stable per-install identifier used to key cloud saves, so it is never published in any form - not hashed, not truncated, because a stable pseudonym is still a correlatable identifier.

**Returns:** A view carrying only whether an id exists.

<a id="gamedataprivacy--redactlocalmusicpath"></a>

### `static string RedactLocalMusicPath(string fullPath)`

Reduces an imported music file's path to its file name.

**Parameters**

- `fullPath`: The absolute path the game stored for a locally imported track. The directory part leaks the OS account name and the player's folder layout, so only the leaf survives.

**Returns:** The file name, or an empty string when the path is null, empty, or ends in a separator. Handles both separators regardless of the running OS, because a save file written on Windows can be read on macOS.

## `GameDataSection`

enum · `CwyLs.ModLoader.Core.Data.GameDataSection` · assembly `CwyLs.ModLoader.Core` · mod API

One addressable area of the player's save data. The names mirror the properties on the game's `Bulbul.SaveDataManager`, which is the single root of everything the player owns. The mapping from each `SaveDataManager.Save*`/`Delete*` method name to a section is [`SaveMethodRules.TryDataSection`](#savemethodrules--trydatasection): plain strings, so it stays Unity-free and is unit-tested against the game's method list.

Values are stable: the JSON snapshot and [`GameDataChanged`](#gamedatachanged) both name sections by their enum name, so renaming one is a breaking change for modders and sidecar tools.

## `GameDataSignals`

static class · `CwyLs.ModLoader.Core.Data.GameDataSignals` · assembly `CwyLs.ModLoader.Core`

Which game observable firings ([`GameSignal`](CwyLs.ModLoader.Core.Events.md#gamesignal)) the data bus reports as a change, and under which section and reason. Pure, so the set is unit-tested.

The set is exactly what the data bus used to subscribe to itself, so its `DATA ... changed reason=event:<Name>` lines are unchanged: the six pomodoro transitions and the two music observables. Pause, unpause, the per-frame timer update and the shuffle toggles are typed events for mods but not data changes.

The section and change reason for a signal, or false when the data bus ignores it.

**Parameters**

- `signal`: The observable that fired.
- `section`: The section it changes, or [`GameDataSection.Unknown`](#gamedatasection--unknown).
- `reason`: The change reason, e.g. `event:OnPlayMusic`, or empty.

<a id="gamedatasnapshot"></a>

## `GameDataSnapshot`

sealed class · `CwyLs.ModLoader.Core.Data.GameDataSnapshot` · assembly `CwyLs.ModLoader.Core` · mod API

A point-in-time copy of everything the bus publishes, in one object. Written to `BepInEx/data/snapshot.json` so out-of-process tools (an LLM sidecar, a dashboard, a stream overlay) can read the player's state without loading into the game process.

Every field is optional in the sense that a section the game has not loaded yet is `null`; consumers must handle that rather than assume presence. Sections that are lists are never null, only empty.

[`GameDataSnapshot.SchemaVersion`](#gamedatasnapshot--schemaversion) is bumped whenever a field is removed or changes meaning. Adding a field is not a version bump, so readers must ignore unknown keys.

The schema version this class produces. See the remarks for the contract.

<a id="igamedataprovider"></a>

## `IGameDataProvider`

interface · `CwyLs.ModLoader.Core.Data.IGameDataProvider` · assembly `CwyLs.ModLoader.Core`

Extension point that lets any mod publish its own section onto the same bus. Registered providers are captured whenever a snapshot is taken and land under [`GameDataSnapshot.Extra`](#gamedatasnapshot--extra), keyed by [`IGameDataProvider.SectionName`](#igamedataprovider--sectionname).

[`IGameDataProvider.Capture`](#igamedataprovider--capture) is called on Unity's main thread while a snapshot is being built, so it may touch the engine - but it is on the frame budget: keep it to reading fields you already hold. Return plain data (primitives, strings, enums, lists, dictionaries, or simple objects with public properties); the serializer walks it reflectively and gives up below a fixed depth, so do not hand back live game objects.

A provider that throws is logged and skipped for that snapshot: one bad mod cannot stop the rest of the bus from publishing.

<a id="igamedataprovider--sectionname"></a>

### `string SectionName { get; }`

Stable key this provider's data appears under in [`GameDataSnapshot.Extra`](#gamedatasnapshot--extra). Namespace it like a mod id (e.g. `mymod.mood`) so two mods cannot collide. Must be non-empty.

<a id="igamedataprovider--capture"></a>

### `object Capture()`

Produces this provider's current data, or `null` to publish nothing this time. Must not block.

<a id="jsonwriter"></a>

## `JsonWriter`

static class · `CwyLs.ModLoader.Core.Data.JsonWriter` · assembly `CwyLs.ModLoader.Core`

A small reflective object-to-JSON writer, built on [`MiniJson`](CwyLs.ModLoader.Core.md#minijson)'s escaping and number formatting. It exists because the snapshot has to be emitted from a Unity Mono plugin (no System.Text.Json) and from a net10.0 unit test with identical output, and because [`IGameDataProvider`](#igamedataprovider) lets mods hand us arbitrary objects we cannot type ahead.

Rules, all of which the unit tests pin down:

- `null` becomes `null`.
- `UInt64` becomes a JSON *string*. The game mints ids from `DateTime.Now.Ticks` (~6.4e17), far above the 2^53 a JavaScript or JSON-float reader can hold exactly, so emitting them as numbers would silently corrupt every todo and note id.
- `DateTime` and `DateTimeOffset` become ISO-8601 with millisecond precision; a UTC `DateTime` gets `Z`, a local one its offset, an unspecified one neither.
- Enums become their name; `Guid` and `TimeSpan` become strings.
- Non-finite floats become `null`, because `NaN` is not JSON.
- Anything else is walked reflectively: public readable instance properties and public instance fields, keys camel-cased. Key order follows reflection order and is not part of the contract.

Depth is capped at [`JsonWriter.MaxDepth`](#jsonwriter--maxdepth) and objects already on the current path are replaced by [`JsonWriter.CycleMarker`](#jsonwriter--cyclemarker), so a mod handing back a live, self-referencing game object cannot hang the writer.

<a id="jsonwriter--cyclemarker"></a>

### `const string CycleMarker = "<cycle>"`

Emitted in place of a value that refers back into its own path.

<a id="jsonwriter--depthmarker"></a>

### `const string DepthMarker = "<max-depth>"`

Emitted in place of a value nested deeper than [`JsonWriter.MaxDepth`](#jsonwriter--maxdepth).

<a id="jsonwriter--maxdepth"></a>

### `const int MaxDepth = 12`

How deep the walker nests before giving up.

<a id="jsonwriter--write"></a>

### `static string Write(object value, Action<string> onError = null)`

Serialises `value` to a compact JSON document.

**Parameters**

- `value`: Anything; see the type's remarks for how each shape is written.
- `onError`: Called with a one-line description whenever a member cannot be read (a property getter threw). The member is then omitted. Pass the plugin's logger so a broken provider is visible in LogOutput instead of silently producing a short document.

<a id="notepageview"></a>

## `NotePageView`

sealed class · `CwyLs.ModLoader.Core.Data.NotePageView` · assembly `CwyLs.ModLoader.Core` · mod API

One page of the in-game notebook.

The game keeps only the three most recently touched pages in memory (`NoteDataV2.PageCache`); every other page's body lives on disk until it is opened. [`NotePageView.Text`](#notepageview--text) is therefore populated only when the body was already available or the adapter was allowed to read it - [`NotePageView.TextAvailable`](#notepageview--textavailable) says which, and the `Data.IncludeNoteText` config switch can turn the body off entirely for privacy. [`NotePageView.Title`](#notepageview--title) always comes from the game's cheap title index and is always present.

<a id="notepageview--textavailable"></a>

True when [`NotePageView.Text`](#notepageview--text) holds the real body. False means "not loaded or withheld", which is not the same as "the page is empty".

<a id="savemethodrules"></a>

## `SaveMethodRules`

static class · `CwyLs.ModLoader.Core.Data.SaveMethodRules` · assembly `CwyLs.ModLoader.Core`

Which `Bulbul.SaveDataManager` methods the framework hooks, and what each one means to its two consumers: the typed event bus (`SaveSection`) and the data bus (`GameData.Changed`). Pure, so the method set and the section table are unit-tested against the game's real method list.

There is exactly one Harmony postfix per hooked method (`SaveDataHook` in the game adapter), and both consumers listen to it. Earlier, the event bus and the data bus each patched the `Save*` family themselves, so every save ran two postfixes.

Names ending in `Throttled` are never hooked: they only reserve a save that arrives shortly as the real method, and reporting both would announce one change twice.

<a id="savemethodrules--deleteprefix"></a>

### `const string DeletePrefix = "Delete"`

Prefix of a method that deletes save data.

<a id="savemethodrules--saveprefix"></a>

### `const string SavePrefix = "Save"`

Prefix of a method that writes a save section.

<a id="savemethodrules--throttledsuffix"></a>

### `const string ThrottledSuffix = "Throttled"`

Suffix of a method that only schedules a later save.

<a id="savemethodrules--mappednames"></a>

### `static IReadOnlyCollection<string> MappedNames { get; }`

Every method name the section table knows, for diagnostics and tests.

<a id="savemethodrules--eventsection"></a>

### `static string EventSection(string methodName)`

The section name a `SaveSection` event carries: the method name without its `Save` prefix, e.g. `SaveTodoList` becomes `TodoList`. A name that is only the prefix, or does not start with it, is returned unchanged.

**Parameters**

- `methodName`: The save method's name.

<a id="savemethodrules--ishooked"></a>

### `static bool IsHooked(string methodName)`

True for a method the shared hook patches: a `Save*` or `Delete*` method that is not a `*Throttled` reservation. The caller still filters out abstract and open generic methods, which Harmony cannot patch.

**Parameters**

- `methodName`: A public instance method name of `SaveDataManager`.

<a id="savemethodrules--issave"></a>

### `static bool IsSave(string methodName)`

True for a hooked method that writes a section, which is what the event bus reports as a `SaveSection`. `Delete*` methods feed the data bus only.

**Parameters**

- `methodName`: The hooked method's name.

<a id="savemethodrules--trydatasection"></a>

### `static bool TryDataSection(string methodName, out GameDataSection section)`

The data section a hooked method changes. False when the table does not name the method (a game update probably added it); `section` is then [`GameDataSection.Unknown`](#gamedatasection--unknown).

**Parameters**

- `methodName`: The hooked method's name.
- `section`: The section, or [`GameDataSection.Unknown`](#gamedatasection--unknown).

<a id="snapshotserializer"></a>

## `SnapshotSerializer`

static class · `CwyLs.ModLoader.Core.Data.SnapshotSerializer` · assembly `CwyLs.ModLoader.Core`

Turns a [`GameDataSnapshot`](#gamedatasnapshot) into the JSON document written to `BepInEx/data/snapshot.json`. A one-line wrapper over [`JsonWriter`](#jsonwriter) on purpose: it is the named, stable entry point mods and sidecars are told about, while the walker underneath stays free to change.

<a id="snapshotserializer--tojson"></a>

### `static string ToJson(GameDataSnapshot snapshot, Action<string> onError = null)`

Serialises a snapshot.

**Parameters**

- `snapshot`: The snapshot; must not be null.
- `onError`: Optional sink for per-member failures (see [`JsonWriter.Write`](#jsonwriter--write)). A member that cannot be read is omitted rather than aborting the document.

**Exceptions**

- `ArgumentNullException`: `snapshot` is null.
